question: How many new-mover leads are in Lancaster County?
html:
New-Mover Leads in Lancaster County

The context has no Lancaster-specific new-mover count. The only figure is roughly 2,300 arm's-length residential sales a month across the nine-county PA core. At the plan's assumed mail response rate, that works out to about 23 leads a month for the whole core (est.), not for Lancaster alone (Punctual Pros ad plan).

What the data shows

  • County deed records show about 2,300 arm's-length residential sales a month in the PA core and about 1,150 on the Jersey Shore. Each sale is a household that must choose HVAC, plumbing and electrical providers within months (Punctual Pros ad plan, Oct 6, 2026).
  • One in three of those PA buyers bought a pre-1980 home (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • The plan assumes a mail lead rate of 1.0% per piece. That is set deliberately below the ANA prospect response benchmark of 4-5% (Punctual Pros ad plan caveats).
  • Lancaster is one of nine core counties, alongside York, Dauphin, Cumberland, Berks, Lebanon, Franklin, Adams and Perry. It hosts a confirmed tri-brand site on Running Pump Rd (Punctual Pros market profile, Sep 24, 2026).
ScopeNew movers per monthLeads at 1.0% (est.)
PA core, nine counties~2,300~23
Jersey Shore~1,150~11.5
Lancaster CountyNot in contextNot in context

Why the county split is missing

  • The ad plan reports deed counts only at the core and Jersey Shore level.
  • The market profile does not give Lancaster's household count, so even a share-of-households split cannot be computed from the context.
  • The building-permits snapshot measures new construction, not resales. Lancaster also does not appear in the rows shown, so it cannot stand in for move-ins (Census building permits, Sep 2026).
  • The 1.0% rate is a planning assumption. Actual lead counts depend on the week 2 and week 4 mail-drop reads against the 10% new-mover holdout (Punctual Pros ad plan).

What would answer it

  • Lancaster County deed records, filtered to arm's-length residential sales, for the last 30 to 90 days.
  • The same records flagged by year built, to size the pre-1980 subset for the Ben Franklin offer.
  • ServiceTitan tracking-number and QR results from mail drop 1, filtered to Lancaster zips, to replace the 1.0% assumption with an observed rate.

Next actions

  1. Pull the Lancaster split from the deed-record source already behind the ~2,300 core figure. Report monthly sales and the pre-1980 share.
  2. Tag every mail piece by county in ServiceTitan, so the week 4 read gives Lancaster leads and booked jobs separately.
  3. Compare Lancaster's observed lead rate with the 1.0% assumption after postcard #2. Reset the mail budget for the county if the gap is large.
  4. Add Lancaster households to the market profile, so future county estimates can be checked against a household base.

# New-Mover Leads in Lancaster County

The context has no Lancaster-specific new-mover count. The only figure is roughly 2,300 arm's-length residential sales a month across the nine-county PA core. At the plan's assumed mail response rate, that works out to about 23 leads a month for the whole core (est.), not for Lancaster alone (Punctual Pros ad plan).

## What the data shows

- County deed records show about 2,300 arm's-length residential sales a month in the PA core and about 1,150 on the Jersey Shore. Each sale is a household that must choose HVAC, plumbing and electrical providers within months (Punctual Pros ad plan, Oct 6, 2026).
- One in three of those PA buyers bought a pre-1980 home (Punctual Pros ad plan).
- The plan assumes a mail lead rate of 1.0% per piece. That is set deliberately below the ANA prospect response benchmark of 4-5% (Punctual Pros ad plan caveats).
- Lancaster is one of nine core counties, alongside York, Dauphin, Cumberland, Berks, Lebanon, Franklin, Adams and Perry. It hosts a confirmed tri-brand site on Running Pump Rd (Punctual Pros market profile, Sep 24, 2026).

| Scope | New movers per month | Leads at 1.0% (est.) |
|---|---|---|
| PA core, nine counties | ~2,300 | ~23 |
| Jersey Shore | ~1,150 | ~11.5 |
| Lancaster County | Not in context | Not in context |

## Why the county split is missing

- The ad plan reports deed counts only at the core and Jersey Shore level.
- The market profile does not give Lancaster's household count, so even a share-of-households split cannot be computed from the context.
- The building-permits snapshot measures new construction, not resales. Lancaster also does not appear in the rows shown, so it cannot stand in for move-ins (Census building permits, Sep 2026).
- The 1.0% rate is a planning assumption. Actual lead counts depend on the week 2 and week 4 mail-drop reads against the 10% new-mover holdout (Punctual Pros ad plan).

## What would answer it

- Lancaster County deed records, filtered to arm's-length residential sales, for the last 30 to 90 days.
- The same records flagged by year built, to size the pre-1980 subset for the Ben Franklin offer.
- ServiceTitan tracking-number and QR results from mail drop 1, filtered to Lancaster zips, to replace the 1.0% assumption with an observed rate.

## Next actions

1. Pull the Lancaster split from the deed-record source already behind the ~2,300 core figure. Report monthly sales and the pre-1980 share.
2. Tag every mail piece by county in ServiceTitan, so the week 4 read gives Lancaster leads and booked jobs separately.
3. Compare Lancaster's observed lead rate with the 1.0% assumption after postcard #2. Reset the mail budget for the county if the gap is large.
4. Add Lancaster households to the market profile, so future county estimates can be checked against a household base.
